title: Higher-order monotone variational inequalities: complete operator jets and tangential residual
summary: Solve the monotone VI $0\in F(z)+N_K(z)$ by returning a feasible point with small tangent residual.

description_paragraphs: Solve the monotone VI $0\in F(z)+N_K(z)$ by returning a feasible point with small tangent residual.

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: Assume $F\in C^{p-1}$ and $\|\mathrm{D}^{p-1}F(u)-\mathrm{D}^{p-1}F(v)\|\le L_p\|u-v\|$ on a neighborhood of $K$, with $p\ge2$ fixed.
The feasible domain is nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$; for saddle problems, $K=X\times Y$.

model.parameter_domain_description: $D_K$: positive real; $L_p$: positive real; $d$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $p$: integer at least 2. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.
description_paragraphs: The set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(K)\le D_K$. Queries and outputs lie in $K$. Differentiability conditions hold on a neighborhood of $K$.

Fix an integer $p\ge2$. The operator $F$ is monotone, meaning $\langle F(u)-F(v),u-v\rangle\ge0$; moreover, $F\in C^{p-1}$ and $\|\mathrm{D}^{p-1}F(u)-\mathrm{D}^{p-1}F(v)\|_{\rm op}\le L_p\|u-v\|_2$.
These conditions ensure existence of a solution. Derivative tensors use the multilinear operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm.

This nonnegative error uses the declared Euclidean geometry.
For a closed convex set $K$, define $N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0,\ \forall u\in K\}$ for $z\in K$, and $\operatorname{dist}(0,S)=\inf_{v\in S}\|v\|_2$.

notes: Let $T$ denote the outer iteration count. Lemma 5.4 and (22)-(23) sum all inner-solver calls to obtain total inner cost $O(T)$. The counted object is a full jet call, so outer iterations alone are insufficient. Bound the source initial distance to a solution by the domain diameter $D_K$.
evidence.applicability_review: Source R_0=||x0-x*|| <= $D_K$, not a new diameter assumption. Full operator jet through p-1; same-point tangent certificate. All nested F calls counted.
